text:
julia_support: Customer opened an escalation: intermittent mTLS failures to Private control plane after deploying a new NGFW/egress stack. Control plane logs show `tls: handshake timeout` and occasional `tls: bad certificate`.
kevin_net: Can you paste the exact control plane log lines and any `openssl s_client` output they ran? Need topology: NAT type, DNS changes, whether there's an SSL inspection proxy.
mike_ops: From customer: "[2026-03-11T09:21:15Z] tls: TLS handshake error from 10.12.4.22: remote error: tls: bad certificate" then later "[2026-03-11T09:21:21Z] tls: handshake timeout". They attached a pcap showing ClientHello retransmits.
julia_support: Customer ran `openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.example:443 -servername control.private.redwood.example -alpn h2 -msg` — server never sends ServerHello. Their tcpdump shows ClientHello in two TLS records: first 256 bytes, then rest (fragmented).
alex_r: Fragmented ClientHello + an active TLS inspector that reserializes CH can drop extensions. Do we see SNI/ALPN disappear after the NGFW?
mike_ops: Yes — pcaps show ClientHello from client contains ALPN `h2,http/1.1`, but the packet arriving at our control plane is missing ALPN and is padded to 768 bytes. The inspector appears to re-encapsulate and pad the CH.
kevin_net: Also interesting: their edge has DNS64 enabled and SD-WAN enforced MTU 1200, plus symmetric NAT. Combined, the CH fragmentation and a rewriter that reassembles incorrectly could strip ALPN and the certificate request flow.
julia_support: I requested repro steps: (1) `openssl s_client -msg -connect control.private.redwood.example:443 -servername control.private.redwood.example` from behind NGFW and from a bypass host; (2) `tcpdump -n -s0 -w pre.pcap host control.private.redwood.example and port 443` on both sides of the NGFW; (3) `curl --http1.1 -v --resolve control.private.redwood.example:443:203.0.113.45 https://control.private.redwood.example/health`.
mike_ops: They ran them. Comparison shows ALPN present pre-inspection, absent post-inspection. CH also swapped extension ordering and was padded. The inspector advertises it does ClientHello padding to 768 bytes to reduce fingerprinting.
alex_r: Customer-facing immediate mitigations to propose:
• Configure SSL passthrough for control.private.redwood.example (bypass inspection) :point_right: recommended
• Disable ClientHello padding for that FQDN
• Temporarily allow direct egress to control plane IPs or preserve NAT port mapping (avoid symmetric NAT)
• Disable DNS64 translation for control plane hostnames (use A/AAAA records)
kevin_net: Can we do any server-side workaround? A tolerant fallback to accept missing ALPN and treat as HTTP/1.1 could help but touches routing/selection logic.
alex_r: I don't want to change the default behavior across customers. We can offer a short-lived per-customer fallback flag (accept missing ALPN) but must gate and log it heavily. I'll open an internal ticket.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: tls/handshake debug logging -> staging (ETA 1h)
mike_ops: For troubleshooting ask them to provide: full pcaps from pre/post NGFW, hex dumps of ClientHello, and `openssl s_client -msg` outputs. Also please run a test with MTU set to 1500 to check if fragmentation is the root cause.
julia_support: I sent the recommended text and asked them to open a temporary bypass tomorrow morning for a subset of hosts. They've agreed to enable a passthrough for three nodes for 2 hours so we can confirm.
kevin_net: If passthrough fixes it we close the loop: NGFW mutation is root cause and permanent config change required. If it fails, escalate to infra for deeper TLS reassembly issues.
julia_support: Noted — follow-up scheduled for 1907012000 (tomorrow morning). I'll update the customer and attach the log request. :thumbsup:
